name: emma-other
comment: The emma guest (app/src/PrismEmma.lex.tex) answers three requests, each a verb, a line end and a body. 'check' and a document answers 'malformed', or 'conforms' or 'violates' with assertion ids. 'read' and a document answers 'malformed', 'other' when the document is not one the writer writes, else its lines. 'input' and lines answers the document those lines describe, 'invalid' when the lines are not in the grammar, or 'refused' and the checker's report when the document they describe would break an assertion: the writer never answers a document its own checker faults. The lines: 'ns <uri>' first, when the payload has a namespace; 'stage <id>' opens an interpretation inside emma:derivation, 'best <id>' the interpretation (or emma:one-of member) that is a child of emma:emma, 'choice <id>' an emma:one-of; 'set <annotation> <value>' gives the open element an emma: annotation; 'from <id>' or 'from <id> composite' an emma:derived-from; 'field <name> <text>' a payload element, which 'set' lines then annotate and 'attr <name> <value>' lines give attributes ('attr xmlns <uri>' its own namespace, 'attr xml:<name> <value>' an attribute of XML's own); 'literal <text>' an emma:literal. No document of the Recommendation that has the writer's shape carries an 'attr' line, so no vector here holds that line. Values write a backslash, line feed, carriage return and tab as two characters. This set: 'read' of the Recommendation's documents of sections 2 to 4.1 that do not have the writer's shape (groups, sequences, lattices, nested payloads, endpoint and grammar references): 'other', or 'malformed' for the ones not well-formed as published.
